Likely impact: one-field tuple/newtype structs are the affected category. Serde derive intentionally emits `deserialize_newtype_struct` for them, whereas multi-field tuple structs use `deserialize_tuple_struct`. csv implements both entry points as sequence-oriented operations, but the newtype path invokes `Visitor::visit_newtype_struct`, which recursively deserializes exactly one inner value. Consequently, a one-field tuple/newtype wrapper around a sequence-like type (for example `struct Row(Vec<String>)`, or wrappers around arrays/tuples) can produce different behavior from an ordinary one-field named struct or multi-field tuple struct when the serde version changes derive dispatch or visitor handling. Migration should avoid relying on a one-field tuple wrapper for CSV rows; use a named struct for header-based records, a multi-field tuple struct for positional records, or explicitly implement `Deserialize`/use a custom `deserialize_with` when wrapper semantics are required.
